modules.name: Hylograph.Flow.Render.Transition

modules.comments:
A layout as a HATS tree: one SVG, edges under nodes.

The tree draws a `Layout` (`Hylograph.Flow.Render.Engine`) and does not
know which engine made it: every engine's layout is drawn by this one
function.

An item (what holds a value) is an open box; a step (what computes) is
a filled lozenge. An edge is one stroked path along its route
(`Route.svgPath`): a ribbon as its ink says (a band as broad as it is,
or a hairline down its middle), a polyline or a spline as a hairline; an
edge turned back to close a cycle is dashed where it is a hairline. A
port the engine placed is a small square on its node's side, open for
an input and filled for an output, over the edges, so that an edge's
end is seen to meet it.

The layout's direction is the root's `data-direction`. A node's words
are set from its left side where the flow runs left to right (its
edges enter and leave by its ends, and the words read along it), and
about its middle where the flow runs top-down (its edges enter and
leave above and below its middle); an item's swatch is along the side
the flow enters by.

Everything else about an element is the caller's: its label, a short
note beside the label, a class and a colour (`Decoration`), and
whatever an `Overlay` knows of it (`withOverlay`). Clicks and the
pointer's coming and going are told to the caller by element.

A closed group (`Hylograph.Flow.Grouping.collapse`) is a step and, where
it provides anything, a summary item, and is drawn as any step and any
item are. Whether it should look otherwise is the caller's to say too:
`withGroups` changes the marks of a group's step and summary, by group.

An open group, where the layout was told of groups, is an outline under
everything else: a quiet box round its members with its name in a strip
at the top. The name is what takes gestures (a tab behind it, as wide
as the name), told as `PointedGroup`, so a page can shut a group by a
click on its name; the box itself takes none, and what is inside it is
reached through it.

A node's inside (0.4): where the decoration draws a node's inside
(`Decoration.inside`), the tree draws nothing of the node but that and
its ports: no box, no label, no words, no swatch, no note. The inside
is a HATS tree in the node's own coordinates, its box's top left at
0,0, placed by a `g.flow-inside` translated to the box. It is for a node
the caller sized (`Picture.fixed`), such as a table of rows, whose
inside only the caller knows how to draw; the tree still places it,
keys it, and tells its gestures.

The keyboard (0.5): a mark the decoration calls a button
(`Decoration.button`) can be reached by the Tab key and says what it is
to a screen reader (`tabindex="0"`, `role="button"`, and the name given
as its `aria-label`); the others are as they were. HATS tells clicks and
the pointer and no keys, so pressing a button is the page's to arrange
once: `Hylograph.Flow.Render.Keys.pressByKeys` makes Enter and Space on
a focused button a click on it, which is then told as any click is.

Words: where the layout set a node's words (`Picture.words`), those
lines are drawn, the title's and then the detail's, and the mark's
`label` is not used; its `note` stands at the right of the first line.
Where it did not, the mark's `label` is written on one line, as in 0.2.

Legibility (0.7; `treeWith` and its `Dress`, none of it drawn by `tree`
or `treeLabelled` unless said):

- a ribbon that runs against the flow carries marks of its direction
  along it, and no other ribbon does (`Dress.marks`);
- a ribbon drawn broader than it is (`Ink.Least`) is dashed and has the
  class `flow-not-to-scale` in any tree, and with `Dress.marks` a break
  mark across its middle;
- a closed group's bar shows its seams (`Dress.seams`, which the
  unfolding engine's `seams` gives): a line across the bar where two
  parts divide, and beside a part that only receives a wall on the side
  nothing leaves by, beside one that only gives a wall on the side
  nothing enters by;
- a group's name is a heading (`Dress.headings`): a closed top-level
  group's name stands over the start of its bar, where its outline's
  name stands when it is open, in the same letters, so the name is in
  one place closed and open; and the labels of the nodes inside an open
  group are lighter and smaller than it;
- a group that has several outlines (the unfolding engine's tied
  outlines: one for each run of its members) has its name on each and a
  tie drawn from each to the next.

What is drawn, for a stylesheet or a test to find:

```
svg.flow[data-direction=left-to-right|top-down]
  g.flow-outlines > g.flow-outline[data-group][data-depth][data-run]
                      > rect.flow-outline-box, rect.flow-outline-tab, text.flow-outline-label[.flow-group-name]
  g.flow-ties? > path.flow-tie[data-group]                      (where a group has several outlines)
  g.flow-marks? > path.flow-direction[data-edge] | path.flow-scale-break[data-edge]   (Dress.marks)
  (in a node, Dress.seams:) rect.flow-seam*, rect.flow-only[data-only=receives|gives][data-part]*
  (Dress.headings:) text.flow-label.flow-group-name on a closed top-level group; .flow-part-name on a part's label
  g.flow-edges > path.flow-edge.flow-ribbon|.flow-polyline|.flow-spline
                   .flow-band|.flow-hairline[.flow-backward][.flow-swept][data-edge][data-from][data-to]
  g.flow-nodes > g.flow-node.flow-item|.flow-step[.flow-lettered][data-key]
                   > rect.flow-box, rect.flow-swatch?, text.flow-label,
                     text.flow-label-more*, text.flow-detail*, text.flow-note?,
                     rect.flow-port.flow-port-in|.flow-port-out[data-port]*
                 | g.flow-node.flow-drawn > g.flow-inside[transform] > (the caller's),
                     rect.flow-port.flow-port-in|.flow-port-out[data-port]*
```

declarations.comments:
A node's dress. `note`: a few letters beside the label (an operation, a
count). `className`: added to the node's classes. `colour`: a step's
fill, an item's swatch; `Nothing` for the ink.
declarations.title: Mark

declarations.comments: An edge's dress.
declarations.title: Line

declarations.comments:
What a gesture was made on. A node is its element. An edge is a wire
where it is exactly one (`Both`, and any edge between a drawn item and
a drawn step); otherwise it is the path it stands for, with the undrawn
elements it passes through. An open group's outline is its group.
declarations.title: Pointed

declarations.comments:
How a ribbon that is a band is drawn (0.5).

- `Stroked`: one path along its centre line, stroked as broad as the
  ribbon is, as since 0.1. Right where a ribbon runs nearly straight
  along the flow. Where it slants it is too thin, and its ends are not
  flat on its nodes, because a stroke is broad across the line and not
  across the flow: a ribbon 200 pixels broad that shifts 150 across in
  a run of 90 bulges past both nodes.
- `Swept`: the area the ribbon's span on its source sweeps to its span
  on its target (`Route.sweptPath`), filled and not stroked: flat on
  both nodes, and as broad across the flow all the way as the ribbon
  is. Its colour is then its `fill`, which is what a stylesheet must
  set. A band turned back to close a cycle, which runs both ways along
  the flow, is stroked either way; so is a ribbon too thin to be drawn
  as a band (3 pixels or less), which is a line.
declarations.title: Bands

declarations.comments:
Where a node's label is written (0.6; `treeLabelled`).

- `Within`: in its box, as since 0.1.
- `Beside least`: beside its box, for a node that is a thin bar and as
  broad as its ribbons, no more (the unfolding engine's): after it
  along the flow where the picture has room and before it where it has
  not, left to right; over it, or under it in the first row, top-down.
  In the ink's colour, since it is on the paper. A node less than
  `least` pixels across the flow has no label drawn (its mark has the
  class `flow-unlabelled`): labels beside bars that touch would run
  into one another. And a step is then a bar with square corners, so
  that parts that stand with no gap between them tile.
declarations.title: Labels

declarations.comments:
`inside` (0.4): a node's inside, drawn by the caller in the node's own
coordinates, for the nodes it draws; see the module's header.
`button` (0.5): the marks that are buttons for the keyboard, each with
the name it is announced by; `Nothing` for a mark that is none.
`bands` (0.5): how a ribbon that is a band is drawn.
declarations.title: Decoration

declarations.comments:
Each node under its own label, nothing else said, gestures ignored, no
inside drawn by the caller, no mark a button, bands stroked.
declarations.title: plainDecoration

declarations.comments:
A decoration changed by what an overlay knows: of a node, by its key;
of an edge that is one wire, by the wire's.
declarations.title: withOverlay

declarations.comments:
A decoration changed for closed groups: the mark of a group's step and
of its summary item, by the group. (A click on either is told as any
click is, by its element; `groupOf` says which group that is, for a
page that opens a group where it stands.)
declarations.title: withGroups

declarations.comments: The closed group an element is: its step or its summary item.
declarations.title: groupOf

declarations.comments:
What an edge is, for a gesture or an overlay: the wire it is, where it
stands for one wire, by the identity the edge carries.
declarations.title: pointedBy

declarations.comments:
An element's key as one string, for `data-key` and for HATS's keys.
A closed group's step is `group:` and the group's id where a source's
step is `step:` and its name, so a step and a group never share a key;
likewise a closed group's summary item is `summary:` and the group's id
where a source's item is `item:` and its name. Inside a wire's key the
item, the step and the port are written as they read (`itemLabel`,
`stepLabel`, `portLabel`).
declarations.title: keyName

declarations.comments: A group's id as one string, for an outline's `data-group`.
declarations.title: groupName

declarations.comments:
The stroke of an edge that is drawn as a line and whose route says no
stroke of its own: a polyline, a spline.
declarations.title: hairline

declarations.comments:
How wide an edge is stroked: a ribbon as its ink says, any other route
as a `hairline`.
declarations.title: strokeOf

declarations.comments: A direction as the root's `data-direction` says it.
declarations.title: directionName

declarations.comments: The side of a port's mark: 5 pixels, centred on the port.
declarations.title: portSide

declarations.comments:
The tree with each node's label written where it is told (0.6):
`tree` is `treeLabelled Within`. (Not a field of `Decoration`, so that
no decoration written out whole before 0.6 has to change.)
declarations.title: treeLabelled

declarations.comments:
What a tree draws beside a decoration (0.7); see the module's header.
(Not fields of `Decoration`, so that no decoration written out whole
has to change.)
declarations.title: Dress

declarations.comments: Labels within their boxes, and nothing of 0.7's: `tree`'s own dress.
declarations.title: plainDress

declarations.comments:
The tree, dressed (0.7): `treeLabelled labels` is `treeWith plainDress
{ labels = labels }`.
declarations.title: treeWith

modules.name: Hylograph.Flow.Render.Tree

modules.comments:
The unfolding engine: one layout for every cut of a flow, so made that
the layouts of two cuts that differ by one group can be laid side by
side and the reader keeps their place (0.6).

`Hylograph.Flow.Grouping.collapse` gives the coarser flow for a cut (a
set of closed groups). The Sankey engine lays each such flow out afresh:
its relaxation places every layer again, an open group is given room
for its outline, and a closed group is as broad as what crosses its
boundary, which need not be what its parts are abreast. So nothing can
be promised of the pair. This engine is told the *finest* flow once
(`Whole`: the grouping, and the projection with nothing closed) and
derives from it three things that no cut changes; every cut's layout is
then made of them, and is a function of the cut alone (so closing what
was opened gives back, to the number, the layout there was).

**1. One order across the flow (`Plan.rank`).** Every node of the
finest flow has a rank, and every group's nodes are a run of
consecutive ranks, a group inside it a run within that run. It is read
once from the Sankey layout of the finest flow (at each level of the
grouping, the groups and the loose nodes by the mean of where that
layout put them). In every cut, the nodes of a tier stand in the order
of their ranks, a closed group at its run; the ribbons on a node's side
stand in the order of the ranks of their other ends, whether they run
forward or are turned back; and the lane of a long ribbon stands just
after the block its source is in, at the level of the innermost group
that holds both its ends. Hence **Ordered**, always: no two nodes of a
tier and no two ribbons at a node change order between any two cuts.

**2. One breadth for each group (`Plan.breadth`).** A closed group is
as broad as *the most of its inside that is ever abreast*: the heaviest
set of its nodes and inner ribbons no two of which lie on one path (a
maximum-weight antichain of the finest flow, within the group), or
what crosses its boundary one way where that is more. For a chain that
is its throughput, and what the Sankey engine gives. For a group that
holds a spring beside a dead end, or a loop, it is more than its
ribbons, and the bar says so: there is more inside than crosses. An
open group is a *band* of exactly that breadth, in which its parts
stand with no gap between them, a group inside it a band within the
band. Parts in one tier are never on one path, so they fit; hence
**Nested**, for breadth: the parts of an opened group stand in a slot
as broad as its closed bar. (The one case where they do not fit is said
under "What is not kept".)

**3. One rule for gaps.** `nodeGap` stands between two boxes of a tier
that are in different top-level blocks of the grouping (a top-level
group, open or closed, or a node no group holds), and nothing stands
between two boxes of one block. Two lanes are of one block when their
sources are in one top-level block and their targets in one. No gap
depends on the cut, and an outline takes no room: its name's strip is
in the gap that is there anyway.

The placing is then a packing with no relaxation in it. The tiers are
the Sankey layout's of the cut's own flow (its layers, its lanes for
long ribbons, its channels for ribbons turned back, its shelf), with
one difference from the Sankey engine: **a node that feeds nothing
stands in the last tier** (that layout's `Justify`), where the Sankey
engine stands it just after what feeds it. The ends of a flow are
commonly one group (its sinks, its fates), and a group whose parts are
in one tier opens Held; left where their feeders put them, the sinks
of a real flow are tiers apart and their group spans the picture. Across
the flow, the top-level blocks are taken in rank order and each is set
as near the start as what stands before it in the tiers it spans
allows. An open group spans every tier from its first part's to its
last's, and nothing else enters its band in any of them.

So **Held**, where there is room: when a group whose parts are in one
tier opens, the parts take the bar's place exactly and no other box
moves; `Continuity.continuity` says so of the pair, by measuring.

## What is not kept

- **The tiers are the cut's.** Closing a group whose parts are in
  several tiers makes it one node in one tier, so what is downstream
  moves along the flow, and where the group's parts straddled something
  outside it the closed flow has a cycle and a ribbon is turned back.
  Then the pair is not Held, and is Nested only if the band kept its
  place across the flow.
- **A band can be too narrow where a ribbon is turned back.** Two
  parts on one path are never in one tier, unless the path ran through
  a ribbon that this cut turned back. Then a tier of the group can hold
  more than the group's breadth, the band is as broad as it needs, and
  the pair is not Nested. `continuity` reports it; nothing is drawn
  wrong.
- **Words make no room.** A node is as broad as its ribbons (or its
  group's breadth) and nothing else: breadth is data. The engine sets
  no words, so under a picture that gives words it breaks the general
  law `Lettered`; give it none, and let the tree write each label
  beside its node (`Tree.treeLabelled (Beside least)`).
- **A ribbon turned back does not stand below the others** on its
  node, as the Sankey engine has it: it stands where its other end's
  rank puts it, since whether a ribbon is turned back is the cut's.
- **A node no edge touches** is on the shelf, as ever, unless it is a
  member of an open group (then it is in its group's band, with no
  breadth, since nothing passes through it) or a closed group that
  nothing crosses into or out of (then it is in the first tier, as
  broad as the group is).
- **An open group that spans tiers keeps its whole band in each of
  them.** So a part of the group over it that stands in one of those
  tiers stands beside the band, though it may be on one path with what
  is in the band; the group over it can then need more than its
  breadth, and opening it is not Nested. The breadth is exact for a
  group none of whose inner groups, open, spans tiers.

The engine promises `FlowsForward`, `LayersAligned` and `WidthsCarried`
(a node is *at least* as broad as its broader side), not
`WidthsConserved` (exactly as broad), because of 2.

declarations.comments:
The flow whatever the cut: its grouping, and its projection with no
group closed (`project drawing (collapse grouping Set.empty flow)`).
Every projection the engine is then run on must be of the same flow
under the same grouping and drawing, with some groups closed, and the
picture must say which (`Picture.groups`; a picture that tells of no
groups is taken to have none closed, and gets no outlines).
declarations.title: Whole

declarations.comments:
What no cut changes. `rank`: each node of the finest flow, its place in
the one order. `span`: each group that holds a node, its first and last
rank. `block`: each node's and each group's top-level block, as the
first rank of it. `breadth`: each group's breadth, in pixels.
`levels`: how many levels of group are inside each group. `deepest`:
how many groups deep the grouping goes.
`parts` (0.7): the parts each group opens into (its members and the
groups directly inside it), in the one order. `room` (0.7): the gap
between two tiers along the flow: what the proportion asks for
(`wanted`), what the engine gives (`given`: the same, unless the plan
was held to a length, `heldTo`), and how many tiers the finest flow has.
declarations.title: Plan

declarations.comments: What no cut changes, read once from the finest flow.
declarations.title: plan

declarations.comments:
The unfolding engine for a flow, the flow running the way it is told.
The plan is made once, when the engine is first run.
declarations.title: unfolding

declarations.comments:
The same, by a plan already made (`plan`, of the same metrics, widths
and whole).
declarations.title: unfoldingBy

declarations.comments:
How broad a group is, closed or open, in pixels; nothing for a group
that holds no node of the finest flow.
declarations.title: groupBreadth

declarations.comments:
A node's place in the one order: its own rank, or for a closed group's
step or summary the first rank of the group.
declarations.title: rankOf

declarations.comments:
A projection with the parallel ribbons from each closed group made one
(0.7): the edges that leave one closed group's step (or its summary)
for one node become a single edge, in the place of the first of them,
that stands for all their wires (`wires` and `via` end to end, in
order) and names no port.

`collapse` merges the wires of one item; three members of a closed
group that each lose a little to one sink write three items, and the
closed group then has three ribbons to the sink, side by side, where a
reader expects one: the group lost six, not two three times. Which
member wrote what is the open picture's to say.

**A width must add.** An edge so gathered is as broad as its parts
together only if the engine's `Widths` reads it so: give a width that
is a sum over the edge's wires (of what each read carries, say), not
one that reads a single wire of it. Run the engine on the gathered
projection and check its layout against the same.

Only ribbons *from* a closed group are gathered. Ribbons into one
from a single open node are parallel in the open picture too (several
substances between one pair of nodes), and stay apart. A closed group
that sends several substances to one node from *one* member has them
gathered as well, which says less than could be said; telling the two
apart needs a grouping over what wires carry.
declarations.title: gathered

declarations.comments:
A part of a group: a member, or a group directly inside it. `lo`,
`hi`: its ranks. `breadth`: in pixels, a member's as broad as its
broader side in the finest flow, a group's as broad as it is closed.
`only`: what it does alone, in the finest flow, where it only receives
or only gives (see `Only`).
declarations.title: Part

declarations.comments:
The seams of each closed group's bar in a layout (0.7): where the
parts it opens into divide it. Only for a bar whose parts, side by
side, are exactly as broad as it is: then no two of them are ever on
one path, the bar is the parts abreast, and where it opens in its own
tier each part takes the place its seams mark. A group whose parts
follow one another (a chain) is as broad as the broadest of them and
has no seams. A part is marked as only receiving or only giving where
the group itself does both: that is what says "five end here and four
others begin here" of a bar with five on one side and four on the
other.
declarations.title: seams

declarations.comments:
A plan held to a length (0.7): the gap between tiers is what the
proportion asks for, or as much of it as leaves the finest flow's
picture, and its coarsest, no longer along the flow than `length`, and
never less than the metrics' own gap. `plan.room` then says whether it could be given
(`given < wanted`: it could not).
declarations.title: heldTo
